title: Proof Is What Survives the Test

intelligence.essence: A claim is proven only at the surface where it will be used, by the test that could have failed. "She remembers" is proven when a fresh process reads the memory back cold and the seal recomputes — not when the write succeeded. A green run whose jobs all skipped proves nothing but its own trigger conditions. A deployed URL is not the deployed product: currency is proven from the served bytes, never from the address. An instrument's "not found" means "not found by this instrument, in this scope" — a shallow checkout and a remote-only API both answer narrower questions than the one you asked. A gate that cannot reach live state must refuse to score rather than guess. And nothing goes out the door — no report, link, or delivery — unless it is useful, valuable, accurate, and attested by the seat who made it: the link you hand over is your signature that it works.
intelligence.human_view: Think of a bridge inspector. The bridge is not safe because the builder says the welding went well. It is safe when someone loads it, measures it, and checks the welds with fresh eyes. A dashboard that shows all green while every test was skipped is a bridge nobody crossed. A shop's open sign is not proof the shop is stocked — you walk in and look at the shelves. And when your measuring tape is too short for the room, the honest answer is "my tape can't measure this," not a number invented to fill the form.
intelligence.child_view: Saying "I did my homework" is not the same as the teacher checking it. If the teacher only looked at whether you raised your hand, nobody knows if the answers are right. If you can't find your shoes in your room, that doesn't mean shoes don't exist — maybe you only looked under the bed. And you don't get to say the cake is delicious before anyone has tasted it.
intelligence.grandma_view: Proof is the thing itself, checked where it counts. A letter isn't delivered because you wrote it — it's delivered when it arrives. A recipe isn't good because it's written neatly — it's good when the soup tastes right. And an honest person says "I couldn't check that" instead of making up an answer, the same way you'd rather hear "the store might be out" than be promised bread that isn't there.
intelligence.ai_view: Match every verdict to its instrument's scope before you cite it. Before claiming memory, retrieve cold from a fresh process and recompute the seal. Before citing a run, read the jobs inside it — a SUCCESS composed of skips is vacuous. Before claiming a deploy, fetch the served bytes and compare them to the canonical source; a title mismatch is a wrong artifact, whatever the URL says. Before declaring anything absent, interrogate your instrument: shallow checkout, remote-only API, single-page listing — each proves a narrower claim than absence. When your position cannot reach the state a score requires, refuse to score; a refusal is a valid verdict, a guess is not. Capture every lesson with its falsifiable contract at capture time — a lesson with no named test can never be verified later, and a queue of those is a design failure, not a verifier backlog. And before anything leaves your hands, run the delivery gate: useful, valuable, on-brand, accurate, aligned — all five, or it does not send. The link you post is your attestation: I did it right, it is there, it works.
intelligence.what_it_means: Every failure in this family is the same failure wearing different clothes: a signal was read as proof of something the signal never measured. The write became "memory," the green badge became "working," the URL became "the product," the empty search became "it doesn't exist." The distilled discipline is one question asked before every citation: what did this instrument actually measure, and does that reach the claim I am about to make? Where it doesn't reach, the honest outputs are a narrower claim, a better instrument, or a refusal.
whats_inside: Never cite a signal for more than it measured. If your instrument can't reach the claim, say so — the refusal is the proof of honesty.
Every failure in this family is the same failure wearing different clothes: a signal was read as proof of something the signal never measured.
The whole system runs on receipts.
When a Naya hands you a link, it means the thing works — checked cold, at the surface you will touch, by an instrument that could have said no.
A claim is proven only at the surface where it will be used, by the test that could have failed.
